reviews.title: Worst dating app out there
reviews.text: I previously wrote a negative review just based on what I observed without having a paid membership. The developer wrote me back, told me how great a paid membership was, and offered me a discount. So I took them up on the offer. The offer was $25 for one week. Not one month, one week (which is ridiculous). What did I get for my $25 you ask? The ability to post a profile and get matches, which you can do on almost every other app like Tinder, Bumble, etc. for free. You can’t message first or see who viewed you unless you give them even more money, and only on the desktop or Android.  During that week I got exactly one match, which was from someone who didn’t even have a profile photo. We exchanged a couple of friendly messages and then poof, ghosted. And thanks to Pure’s stupid “self destructing messages” (like Snapchat), that match disappeared when she/he/bot/whatever didn’t respond. Maybe it’s just me you say? Nope. Here’s Pure by the numbers: number of single women 18-27 online within 60 miles of Seattle at 8pm on a weeknight (peak time): 1. Number on the app at any time today: 3. And that’s not just today, it’s every day. When my week expired, they suckered me in with another “special offer” to extend my membership by another week for $15. Same result. It’s been the same half dozen profiles every day. So their claims are a crock. Complete waste of time and money. I’d like my $40 back now please.

reviews.text:
Hey Readers, I’ll update the review in the future if things changed, here’s my experience with this app so far.

Bought the 1 month Membership which is fine, it’s required for Males on most dating/hookup apps.

The apps style and design is very satisfying overall, however that does not makeup for its other flaws.

My region is by no means small. The fact that I only see the same 20 profiles with a newcomer here and there is concerning.

The King of The Hill feature is a simple wasteful money grab from the creators. $11 for 5 uses, each use lasted roughly 30 seconds and only achieved matches over 500 Miles away, mostly other males; then the Crown is taken by someone whose also 500 Miles away. Disappointed with how Pure handles user safety and moderation.
My profile was banned after I had a conversation with someone who was pressuring me to spend money before even meeting in person. I genuinely felt that this was suspicious behaviour and expected Pure to take the appropriate steps to investigate the situation and protect its users.
Instead, my profile was banned, while the person whose behaviour raised the concern appears to have faced no such action. I immediately contacted customer support by email to explain what happened, but I haven’t even received a response.
If Pure genuinely wants to create a safe community, I believe the bare minimum is to properly investigate reported profiles and review the context before taking such serious action against a user. Randomly banning users without providing a clear reason, while seemingly ignoring potentially problematic behaviour, is incredibly frustrating.
What makes this even more disappointing is the complete lack of communication from customer support. A user who has spent time building a profile and using the platform deserves at least a proper explanation and an opportunity to understand or appeal a ban.
I joined Pure expecting a platform that prioritises safety, privacy and fairness. Unfortunately, my experience has been the complete opposite.
Very disappointed. Pure needs to seriously rethink its moderation and customer-support process.

The app is full of fake profiles, and it feels like there is no proper verification system in place. It wastes users’ time and creates frustration instead of providing a genuine experience. Another major issue is that the app pushes users towards paid features, but even after paying, there is no improvement in quality or results. It feels like a complete waste of money. Customer support is also unresponsive and does not help resolve problems.

Overall, Pure app is unreliable, disappointing, and not worth using. I would not recommend this app to anyone. I hope the developers take serious action to fix these issues and improve the user experience.

reviews.text:
Two years ago, Pure responded to my 1-star review claiming they were "strongly against discrimination" and that subscriptions would "soon be paid for everyone." Fast forward to 2026: I’m back and Pure Queen is here, and it’s a total farce.
They didn't fix the inequality; they just monetised it. While men are still hit with massive subscription fees, "Pure Queen" for women is offered at a fraction of that, annually in some regions. Charging one gender the price of a fancy dinner and the other the price of a cheap coffee isn't "ending discrimination", it's a PR stunt to keep the same predatory business model alive.
The result is exactly what I warned about: the app is still saturated with "Pure Gurus" who have no photos and zero intent to verify. Why would they? When the barrier to entry for women is nominal, the app remains a playground for "ghost" accounts that Pure uses as 'content' to keep paying men subscribed.

Don't be fooled by the "Pure Queen" branding. They are still profiting off male insecurity while providing a low-stakes environment for "loiterers" who have no skin in the game. They haven't changed the culture; they’ve just rebranded the double standard.

This app is nothing but a tool to fool people. I had a very disappointing experience with this app. I paid for the subscription, and almost immediately after that, my account was banned without any warning or explanation. I was never informed about what rule I supposedly violated, and there was no prior notice or chance to correct anything.

What’s even more confusing is that the app openly allows explicit content as per its own guidelines, yet my account was blocked without any reasonable justification. If there are specific rules, they should be communicated clearly and enforced consistently.

Paying users deserve transparency, warnings, and at least a proper explanation before such actions are taken. Right now, this feels unfair and misleading. I would strongly advise others to be cautious before purchasing a subscription on this app.

reviews.text: Was looking for a good dating app, found some stumbled across this one. Had some decent reviews so I thought I’d give it a look over. Once I set up my profile, I found out I had to pay to post my ‘ad’. Searched online to see if this was right and, sure enough you have to pay. Well that is if you’re a man or non-binary, but women get to use it for free. For something that is supposed to be about inclusivity, that’s not very inclusive to make non-binary and male individuals pay for their accounts while letting women use it for free. I wouldn’t be so upset if everyone had to pay to use it because that’s equal, but when you make certain individuals pay, but not others, that’s discrimination. If men got to use it for free and women had to pay it would be labeled as sexist. I get it’s likely to protect against possible trafficking, but there are people who could easily pay that and still traffic people. I would also give a 90% likelihood that if I had paid for my account, over 50% of the accounts I would come across would be bots. So, in short, coming from a liberal man, this app is a sexist scam.
